scope: Whole written syllable per cipher group; conservative Latin subset only. Actual group labels are opaque, not letter values. No German or mixed-language model. Not a universal phonological syllabifier.
syllabification: One a/e/i/o/u nucleus per syllable; between nuclei put last consonant with next vowel, earlier consonants close preceding syllable. Exclude j/q/x/y/z, adjacent vowels (including diphthongs), stop-liquid clusters and ch/ph/th. Unknowns/excluded words remain recorded. No claim these cover every medieval pronunciation or morphological boundary.
model: Learn syllable inventory and add0.1 smoothed syllable-bigram transitions with word boundaries from first60% of existing Latin source. No letter substitution or syllable inventory supplied from test. Four annealing starts x5000 proposed moves; injective group-to-syllable map; swap or replace with unused inventory syllable. Best training objective only.
controls: Fresh same-work60-80% region offsets5600/6300/7000. Each600-word block: first400 yields first100 retained words, final200 yields first20 retained words. No fallback/resampling if insufficient. Random opaque one-group-per-syllable encodings, with true group boundaries supplied: this is easier than Voynich segmentation. Three cases. Freeze inferred mappings before test. Gate all3: >=90% resolved syllable accuracy, >=80% group coverage, >=80% whole-word recovery. Unseen groups stay [UNK]. All known-control mappings and failures saved.
manuscript_if_pass: Fixed v70 EVA grouping and v69 context windows; H-trained mapping applied unchanged to H/F, unseen groups unresolved, freeze before output. No manuscript scoring unless all controls pass; syllable output likelihood alone is not semantic evidence.
limits: Restricted written syllables and same source work; synthetic qualification with supplied boundaries. Failure cannot reject syllabic Voynich. Conditional Latin syllabification excludes many actual source words, with coverage reported.
